questions.question: The expenditure of Renu is 120% more than her savings. If her income and expenditure increase by 25% and 30%, respectively, then her savings increase by:
questions.solution:
Given:

Expenditure = 120% more than Savings. 

Income and Expenditure increased by 25% and 30%.

Concept used:

Income = Expenditure + Savings 

Calculation:

Let, the savings be Rs. 100.

Expenditure = 100 + 100 × 120% = Rs. 220

Income = 100 + 220 = Rs. 320

New income = 320 + 320 × 25%

⇒ Rs. 400

New expenditure = 220 + 220 × 30%

⇒ Rs. 286

So, new savings = 400 - 286 = Rs. 114

Now, her savings increased by = {{114- 100} over 100} times 100\%

⇒ 14%

∴ Her savings increased by 14%.

questions.question: The LCM and HCF of two numbers are 3564 and 81, respectively. If the numbers are 324 and x, then what is the sum of the digits of x?
questions.solution:
Given:

LCM = 3564, HCF = 81

The numbers are 324 and x.

Concept used:

LCM × HCF = The Product of two numbers

Calculation:

According to the concept,

324 × x = 3564 × 81

⇒ x = (3564 × 81)/324

⇒ x = 891

Now, the sum of the digits of x = 8 + 9 + 1 = 18

∴ The sum of the digits of x is 18.

questions.question: A boat running downstream covers a distance of 12 km in 30 minutes and while running upstream at the same speed, it covers the same distance in 36 minutes. What is the speed (in km/h) of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
Given:

At downstream, covers a distance of 12 km in 30 minutes 

At upstream, at the same speed, covers 12 km in 36 minutes.

Concept used:

Upstream speed = (B - R) km/h

Downstream speed = (B + R) km/h

Where, B = Speed of the boat in still water

R = Speed of the stream

Time × Speed = Distance

Calculation:

Let, the speed of the boat in still water and that of the stream be B and R km/h respectively.

According to the question,

(B + R) × 30/60 = 12

⇒ (B + R) = 12/0.5

⇒ (B + R) = 24 ....(1)

(B - R) × 36/60 = 12

⇒ (B - R) = 12 × 60/36

⇒ (B - R) = 20 ....(2)

Now, (1) + (2),

B + R + B - R = 24 + 20

⇒ 2B = 44

⇒ B = 44/2 = 22 km/h

∴ The speed of the boat in still water is 22 km/h.

questions.question: The average of eight consecutive even numbers is 65. If the next four consecutive even numbers are included, then what is the average of all the numbers?
questions.solution:
Concept used:

Consecutive even numbers are (x - 2), x, (x + 2) etc.

**Formula:**

Total = Average × Number of entities

Calculation:

Let, the consecutive even numbers be (x – 6), (x – 4), (x – 2),

x, (x + 2), (x + 4), (x + 6), (x + 8).

According to the question,

⇒ x – 6 + x – 4 + x – 2 + x + x + 2 + x + 4 + x + 6 + x + 8 = 65 × 8

⇒ 8x + 8 = 520

⇒ 8x = 512

⇒ x = 512/8 = 64

Last number of the series = (x + 8) = 64 + 8 = 72

Now, next four even numbers are 

(x + 10), (x + 12), (x + 14), (x + 16) = 74, 76, 78, 80

Sum (74, 76, 78, 80) = 308

Now, the number of terms in the series

⇒ Previous 8 consecutive even numbers + Next four consecutive even numbers

⇒ 8 + 4 = 12

Now, the average of all the numbers

⇒ (Sum of previous 8 consecutive even numbers + Sum of next consecutive even numbers)/Number of terms in series

⇒ {(65 × 8) + 308}/12

⇒ 69

∴ The average of all the numbers is 69.

questions.question: A man can row at 9 km/h in still water. It takes him equal time to go 33 km downstream and to go 21 km upstream. Find the speed of the stream (in km/h).
questions.solution:
Given:

In still water, speed = 9 km/h.

Time for 33 km downstream = Time for 21 km upstream

Concept used:

Upstream speed = (B - R) km/h

Downstream speed = (B + R) km/h

Where, B = Speed of the boat in still water

R = Speed of the stream

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculation:

Let the speed of the stream be R km/h.

Upstream speed = (9 - R) km/h

Downstream speed = (9 + R) km/h

According to the question,

33/(9 + R) = 21/(9 - R)

⇒ 11/(9 + R) = 7/(9 - R)

⇒ 63 + 7R = 99 - 11R

⇒ 18R = 36

⇒ R = 36/18

⇒ R = 2

∴ The speed of the stream is 2 km/h.

questions.question: A certain sum amounts to ₹ 7485 after 3 years and to ₹ 9960 after 8 years at the same rate per cent per annum at simple interest. On simple interest, what will be the amount (in ₹) of the same sum after 7 years at double the earlier rate of interest?
questions.solution:
Given:

An amount to ₹ 7485 after 3 years at SI

The same amount to ₹ 9960 after 8 years at SI

In both cases, rate of interest is same. 

Concept used:

Simple Interest, SI = (P × R × T)/100

Amount = P + SI

Where, P = Principal amount; R = Rate of interest per year;

T = Time 9in years)

Calculation:

Interest in (8 - 3) i.e. 5 years = 9960 - 7485 = ₹ 2475

Interest per year = 2475/5 = ₹495

Let, the principal amount and the rate of interest be ₹ P and R% respectively.

According to the question,

(P × 1 × R)/100 = 495

⇒ PR/100 = 495 ---(1)

According to the question,

P + (P × 3 × R)/100 = 7485

⇒ P + 3PR/100 = 7485 ---(2)

P + (P × 8 × R)/100 = 9960

⇒ P +8PR/100 = 9960 ---(3)

Now, (2) + (3),

⇒ (P + 3PR/100) + (P +8PR/100) = 7485 + 9960

⇒ 2P + 11PR/100 = 17445 ---(4)

Substituting equation (1) in equation (4),

⇒ 2P + (11 × 495) = 17445

⇒ 2P = 17445 - (11 × 495)

⇒ 2P = 12000

⇒ P = 6000

Putting P = 6000 in equation (1),

(6,000 × R)/100 = 495

⇒ R = 495/60 = 8.25

So, the revised simple interest rate = 8.25 × 2 = 16.5%

Now, the amount in 7 years

⇒ 6000 + (6000 × 16.5 × 7)/100

⇒ ₹12930

**∴ The amount becomes ₹12930.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**⇒ Amount for 8 yr = 9960 --- (eq 1)

⇒ Amountthe for 3 yr = 7485 --- (eq 2)

Subtracting (eq 1) and (eq 2) we get

⇒ SI for 5 year = 2475

⇒ SI for 1 year = 495

⇒ SI for 3 year = 1485

We know that Amount = SI + P (for 3 yr)

As per question amount for 3 yr = 7485

⇒ 7485 = 1485 + P

⇒ P = 6000

Using SI formula for 1 year

⇒ Rate% = (495 × 100)/6000 = 8.25%

⇒ 2 × Rate% = 16.5%

Amount for 7 years = SI + P (for 7 yr)

⇒ Amount = [(6000 × 16.5 × 7)/100] + 6000

⇒ Amount = 12930

**∴ The correct answer is Option 1).**

questions.question: Four birds A, B, C, D fly along the circumference of a jungle. They complete one round in 27 minutes, 30 minutes, 45 minutes and 60 minutes, respectively. Since they start together, when will they meet again (in hours) at the starting position?
questions.solution:

Calculation:

questions.question: 12 persons can dig a trench 20 m in length in 8 days. The number of persons required to dig a 30 m trench of the same width and depth in 6 days, is:
questions.solution:
Given:

12 persons dig a trench of 20 m in 8 days.

Concept used:

Total work = Number of workers × Efficiency of each worker × Number of days required

Calculation:

Let, the efficiency of each person be M.

According to the question,

Initial total work = 20

New total work = 30

⇒ 20 = 12 × M × 8

⇒ M = 5/24

Now, the number of persons required = 30 ÷ (5/24 × 6) = 24

**∴ The number of persons required to dig a 30 m trench of the same width and depth in 6 days is 24.**

questions.question: 10 women can complete a work in 15 days. The same work can be completed in 5 days by 15 men. 10 women started the work and after 3 days, 5 men replaced 5 women. In how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
Given:

10 women can complete a work in 15 days. The same work can be completed in 5 days by 15 men. 

10 women started the work and after 3 days, 5 men replaced 5 women.

Concept used:

Total work = Number of workers × Efficiency of each worker × Days to complete the work

Calculation:

Let the total work be 150 units.

Efficiency of each woman = 150 ÷ (10 × 15) = 1 units

Efficiency of each man = 150 ÷ (15 × 5) = 2 units

Work done in 3 days = 10 × 1 × 3 = 30 units

Remaining work = 150 - 30 = 120 units

5 women and 5 men together complete in 1 day = 5 × 2 + 5 × 1 = 15 units

So, the remaining work will be done in = 120/15 = 8 days

Now, the work will be completed = 8 + 3 = 11 days

∴ The work will be completed in 11 days.

questions.question: In an examination, a student requires 35% marks to pass. If Sunita gets 145 marks and fails by 23 marks, then what are the maximum marks of the examination?
questions.solution:
Given:

In an examination, a student requires 35% marks to pass. 

Sunita gets 145 marks and fails by 23 marks.

Calculation:

Passing marks = 145 + 23 = 168

35% of the total marks = 168

Now, the maximum total marks = 168/35%

⇒ 168/0.35 = 480

∴ The maximum marks of the examination is 480.
